notes: Picking a reward no longer frees your mouse from the game, and you now start rooms well away from the walls.
You can switch element at any moment now, mid-cast and while skills are cooling down.
Space jumps, Shift dashes (and dash skills carry you instead of teleporting), the utility skill is on Q, and a Developer tools box on the start page turns the dev panel on.
Under the hood: the torch counts toward the light limit and rooms free their textures when you leave them.
Look at any generated style with ?theme=crypt (or hall, cave) and ?seed=; rooms are built the same way in every browser; early rooms are never one huge enemy.
Under the hood: the practice bot can leave a cleared room through a gate and the balance report covers endless runs.
Runs are now endless and every room is generated: crypts, halls and caves, dark and cluttered, with gates to walk through.
Under the hood: flickering torch-light and textured, tinted walls and floors for the generated dungeon.
Under the hood: sound and effect mapping knows about gates.
Under the hood: the simulation notices when you walk into a gate of a cleared room.
Under the hood: a generator that builds random dark rooms (crypts, halls, caves) from a seed.
Room themes (crypt, hall, cave) are now game data.
The cave rock kit is in the game, ready for the generated dungeon.
Mouse look is fixed: moving the mouse right now turns right, D walks right, and there is an Invert vertical look option on the start page.
The skeletons, zombie, vampire and ghost now stand as tall as the elementals.

Eleven new enemies for the dungeon: skeletons, a skeleton mage, a bone giant, a zombie, a vampire, a ghost, fire and water elementals, a wraith, flying books and a tome guardian. Every enemy is now graded into one cooler, darker palette.
Runs started with saved dev tuning no longer count toward unlocks.
Patch notes and Credits on the main menu; a generated wiki; a bot that can play for the owner when testing.
headless balance bot and report; skills found as rewards are equipped
run flow, screens and the unlock ledger
Six rooms (three forest, three dungeon) and elite enemies with fire auras, burning trails, haste and extra guard.
Twenty skills: eight new ones, and each run starts with a random skill in every slot.
Augments: twelve upgrades that reshape skills, like wider cones, twin streams and exploding fireballs.
Rewards: after each room choose a skill, an augment or a heal, with rarer picks deeper in.
Runs now exist: a seeded eight-room path through forest and dungeon to a boss, with doors that show their reward.
Fights feel like fights: enemies flash when hit and sink when they die, damage numbers float up, and a scripted player can clear a mixed room.
Add your own mobs from the dev panel: upload a model, describe it, spawn it, keep it, export it.
Dev groundwork for adding your own mobs: read, check and prepare uploaded models.
Eleven enemies and two bosses: stumps, treefellows, golems, sprites, wisps, Maw and the Pumpkin Reaper.
Guard stance: tanks cut most damage until you hit their weakness, which breaks the guard.
Enemies now behave: rushers, shooters, tanks, swarms, flyers, chargers, summoners and ambushers.
Enemies can now attack: swipes, slams, shots, charges and summons, each with a ground warning.
The game is playable end to end: move, aim, cast, swap elements and see reactions on training dummies.
Dev panel pages for player, skills, statuses and reactions, run tools, debug drawing and an animation viewer.
On-screen display: crosshair, skills with cooldowns, health, and status icons above enemies.
Spell effects now play: sprite effects for hits, reactions, swaps and dodges.
The player now animates: legs follow movement, casting plays on the upper body, aim tilts the spine.
Twelve starting skills (three per element) and the water, earth, fire and wind combo.
Damage now follows weaknesses, resistances, rocked and guard before it triggers reactions.
Reactions between elements now work: steam, mud, shock chain, magma and the rest.
Burning, soaked, rocked and gusted now work and burning spreads.
Swapping elements, the swap-in bonus, and casting from the mouse buttons.
Skills can now be cast: projectiles, cones, streams, zones, walls, dashes and self buffs.
The player now moves, slides along walls and dodges.
Aiming, the third-person camera and keyboard and mouse input.
Dev panel with a performance page and tuning toolbar.
Data layers and patch validation for tuning values.
The forest clearing: pieces, generated colliders and boundary walls, drawn in the scene.
Chunky render profile and the first scene, with a browser smoke test.
Asset manifest, licence check and asset loader.
Simulation bridge with a worker, and a cap on catch-up after a backgrounded tab.
Simulation core: fixed 60 Hz tick, entities, events, snapshots and a state hash.
Game data schema, loader and validation, with the first data files.
Vector maths and world collision (rays, sweeps, ground).
Seeded random streams for the simulation.
Project started: design spec, build plan and the first converted assets.
